scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated in the Bukcheong region of South Hamgyong Province, rooted in folk beliefs regarding the protective power of lions.
Competitive performances between local towns began in 1930, with prizes of crops used for community welfare.
A transmission committee was formed in 1960 by defectors to South Korea to ensure the survival of the tradition.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performed on the 15th day of the lunar New Year, starting on the 14th night.
It is intended to ward off evil spirits and bring peace.
Children participate by touching the lion to ensure a longer life.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Yun Youn-chun, Kim Su-seok, Byun Young-ho, Dong Young-suk, Yeo Je-sung, and Jeon Jung-sik.
Historically performed in every region of Bukcheong province, with particular fame in Bukcheong-eup, Gaheomyun, and Gutangcheon.
Designated as the 15th Important Intangible Cultural Property of Korea.
